subject.title: fix(setup): validate current OpenClaw package lifecycle

question: Should this repository permanently maintain a CI-composed Gateway candidate built by applying a frozen patch from an unmerged external OpenClaw fork, or wait for a merged upstream commit or official release instead?
rationale: The code can pin commit and patch hashes, but maintainers must decide whether that external provenance and ongoing cross-repository support burden are acceptable for this repository's validation contract.

options.title: Approve the composed candidate policy
options.body: Accept the immutable fork-patch source only with a documented maintainer-owned provenance and removal plan once upstream publishes the equivalent fix.

options.title: Wait for upstream provenance
options.body: Keep this PR open until the required upstream fix is merged or released, then compose from official OpenClaw history and rerun the exact-head proof.

options.title: Limit it to an experimental lane
options.body: Retain the composed build only as clearly non-gating experimental validation and keep supported setup proof on official artifacts.

recommendation.title: Wait for upstream provenance
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open until the required upstream fix is merged or released, then compose from official OpenClaw history and rerun the exact-head proof.
